transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Clara (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (AuroraTech Head of Data), Tom Reynolds (AuroraTech Sec Eng), Priya Sharma (PM)

Summary/Agenda: quick pilot results, SSO issues, audit logs and retention, SOC2 evidence request, next steps.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um this is Samir from Redwood, with Clara our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: good, thanks — busy week but, yeah ready to dig in.
[00:11] Priya: hi all, morning from our side.
[00:14] Tom: yeah, hi. quick note — we had one hiccup with SSO in staging this morning so hoping to get that clarified.

[00:22] Samir: yep, we'll start there. quick TL;DR, today we'll look at the SAML mapping error you saw, audit log retention options, and the SOC 2 pack you asked for. Clara will share the pilot telemetry for the week.

[00:34] Clara: cool, I pulled the usage dashboard — overall throughput is within expected ranges. avg p50 latency from the EU node is 280ms, p95 ~720ms for the 2k token tests. token cost looks as we flagged earlier once you enable prefix caching it drops ~14%. but I can attach the raw sheets. (link: https://redwood.internal/pilot/auroratech/telemetry)
[01:05] Maya: ok thanks. on the SSO — the error says "invalid audience" when we try to login via our IdP. Tom, you saw the same?
[01:12] Tom: yes, we get an audience mismatch, and the assertion doesn't include the email attribute we expected.
[01:18] Clara: right, the dev console shows the SP entity ID is using the workspace slug instead of the full dns we expected. sometimes our metadata generator defaults to the internal id — we should swap to the explicit entity URL. I can update that now if you want.
[01:31] Maya: is that likely what caused the audience error?
[01:33] Clara: yeah most likely. also the attribute mappings — looks like your IdP is sending "mail" instead of "email" which our mapping didn't auto-match, so the email claim was dropped. easy fix in the mapping.
[01:44] Tom: cool. can you also confirm we can restrict login to SSO-only and disable local accounts? we need enforcement.
[01:49] Samir: absolutely, we have a workspace-level policy: SSO-only toggle and enforced SCIM provisioning if you want downstream user provisioning. I'll note that in the action items.
[01:58] Priya: and audit logs — we need to keep them for 1 year, is that possible for the pilot?
[02:04] Clara: out of the box pilot retention is 30 days for detailed audit events, but we can enable extended audit logging for the pilot workspace up to 90 days by flipping the setting. for 1 year we'd recommend export to your SIEM/long-term store — we have an automated export job that pushes logs to S3 or to your Splunk/Datadog forwarder.
[02:23] Tom: we'd prefer S3 export, encrypted with our KMS key. does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:29] Samir: yes, customer-managed key support is available in Private and Dedicated and for hosted we can do envelope encryption with CMKs via the KMS integration in the pilot — I will pull up the doc. (note: link to KMS integration doc shared in chat)
[02:41] Maya: is there any sensitive payload in the audit logs? we only want metadata, not request bodies.
[02:47] Clara: by default audit logs include metadata and request identifiers — full request payload is redacted unless you explicitly enable full request logging. for compliance we typically keep metadata + response codes + user id. we can also configure automatic PII redaction at ingest to strip email/phone values from logs.
[03:03] Tom: how does redaction work? deterministic tokenization or regex? we need to ensure we can prove the redaction method for auditors.
[03:10] Clara: currently we support configurable redaction rules (regex based) and a deterministic hashing plug-in if you want consistent pseudonymization. we can export the redaction config as part of the audit trail for SOC2 evidence.
[03:22] Priya: perfect. what about searchability — if we redact, can we still search by user id?
[03:28] Clara: yes, you can retain a hashed user id column while redacting email, phone in the payload. search by hashed id will work.
[03:34] Maya: ok that addresses a lot. next: SOC2 — we need the evidence package for our procurement team; timeline?
[03:41] Samir: we can send our SOC 2 Type II pack and the security whitepaper today. I will attach the certs and the controls matrix. note that the hosted prod environment is covered; for private deployments we'd need an additional attestation.
[03:56] Tom: make sure the controls matrix includes retention, event logging, change management, and incident response details — procurement expects specifics.
[04:03] Samir: yep, will do. I'll include the control mappings and sample audit logs.
[04:07] Maya: also, is there a way to get a short-lived export of audit logs so we can ingest a 14 day slice into our SIEM for evaluation?
[04:13] Clara: yes — I can run an ad-hoc export and deliver a gzipped CSV that matches your SIEM schema. I'll add a note on the format so you can test ingestion.
[04:22] Tom: great. about data retention — can we set per-route retention windows? e.g., user-chat endpoints purge after 30 days but system prompts keep 1 year.
[04:31] Clara: we have per-model and per-route retention policies; you can set default workspace retention and override per-route. retention enforcement also supports TTL-based deletion jobs. for the pilot we can demonstrate two routes with different policies.
[04:44] Priya: will deleting data remove it from backups as well? auditors care about backups.
[04:49] Samir: deletion jobs trigger backup lifecycle rules — for hosted, backups are retained per our backup retention plan but we have deletion hooks that mark records for removal across snapshots; for enterprise-grade retention guarantees we usually recommend Dedicated/Private where we can meet strict backup deletion SLAs. I'll call that out in the notes.
[05:07] Maya: that makes sense. one more question on logs: we want to ingest audit logs into AWS Lakehouse via S3 and require SSE-KMS with our ARN. is that supported?
[05:16] Clara: yes, we can configure export with SSE-KMS using your key ARN. the export job can be scheduled daily or on-demand. there is a small egress cost which we'll call out on the pricing note.
[05:27] Tom: pricing question — if we export more logs to S3, does that impact our token costs?
[05:31] Samir: export is separate from token billing; token costs come from generation/embedding usage. logs export egress and storage are billed separately. I'll include sample numbers in the pricing doc.
[05:42] Maya: on PII redaction during inference — can we ensure that model outputs never emit email addresses that are in our user base?
[05:50] Clara: we have output filters and custom policy enforcement where you can supply a denylist or a regex-based sanitizer. we can also run a post-generation scrub that checks for exact matches against a hashed list of known user emails and masks them. latency impact is minimal but we'll quantify in the bench run.
[06:06] Priya: speaking of bench runs — we wanted a test that simulates our expected peak: 50 concurrent sessions, average 800 tokens per response, with occasional 6k token context for retrieval. can you replicate that in the pilot?
[06:17] Clara: yes, we can run that. for the large context loads we'd recommend provisioning a slightly bigger instance group for the test day — I will propose parameters and cost delta.
[06:26] Samir: action item: Clara to provide bench config and cost delta; run on 2026-03-20.
[06:31] Maya: ok. one more subtlety — we have regulatory users in the EU; any data residency options for the pilot?
[06:36] Clara: we can pin the pilot workspace to the EU region for all processing and storage. logs export to S3 in eu-west-1 is supported. note that some of the telemetry pages will still route to the control plane in the US unless you opt into the private deployment. but for the pilot we can ensure data-in-region.
[06:54] Tom: good. a minor but real ask — our auditors asked for proof of SSO login attempts and failed assertion logs for the 30-day window. can we provide a sample extract?
[07:03] Clara: yes, extended audit logging will capture failed SAML assertions and reason codes. I'll include a sample file with masked identifiers.
[07:10] Maya: thanks. timeline ok: SOC2 pack tomorrow, SSO metadata to be sent by us on Thursday, Clara to enable logs and export on Wednesday and run bench on Friday.
[07:19] Samir: that's my understanding too. any other blockers?
[07:22] Priya: procurement also asked about contract terms for a 90-day pilot extension if needed — can legal send a redlined MSA?
[07:29] Samir: yes, I'll have legal send a pilot addendum, and I'll include a standard 90-day extension clause.
[07:35] Tom: one small technical follow-up — how are secrets for KMS stored in your control plane? are they resident in HSM?
[07:42] Clara: we use an HSM-backed KMS for master keys in our control plane; customer CMKs are passed through to the cloud provider's KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) and we only store references. we can provide a short architecture diagram in the pack.
[07:56] Maya: ok. thanks everyone.
[08:00] Samir: great. I'll recap after the sync in the notes. thanks for the time.

Recap (verbatim):
- Samir to send SOC2 type II pack + security whitepaper.
- Clara to enable extended audit logs (30->90 days trial) and deliver sample export (S3 + CSV mapping).
- Clara to provide bench config and run perf test 2026-03-20.
- AuroraTech to send SAML IdP metadata and attribute mapping.
- Legal: Samir to circulate pilot addendum with 90-day extension clause.

References shared in chat:
- Pilot telemetry sheet: https://redwood.internal/pilot/auroratech/telemetry
- KMS / encryption notes: https://redwood.internal/security/kms-integration
- SOC2 control mapping: https://redwood.internal/security/soc2-matrix (will attach PDF)

Notes on transcription: occasional dropped words and overlapping talk, some product names transcribed as "redwood" vs "re wood" in one line.
